short_standup.transcript:
[Priya] Scanner lag is still on site three. I think it's firmware, not hardware.
[Marcus] If it's firmware we can ship the rollout and patch after.
[Priya] I want the latency numbers first. Give me until Thursday.

short_one_line.transcript: [Speaker 1] We're not doing per-seat. It punishes the teams we most want using this.

long_technical.transcript:
[Priya] Let's start with site three. The scanner lag is averaging 800 milliseconds now, was 200 last week.
[Marcus] Did anything change on our side?
[Priya] We pushed the firmware update on the 12th. Sites one and two took it fine.
[Dev] Site three is on older hardware. The 2019 units.
[Marcus] So it's the firmware on old hardware, not the firmware.
[Priya] That's my read. I want numbers before I say it out loud to the terminal leads.
[Marcus] What's the exposure if we roll site four on schedule?
[Dev] Site four is all 2022 units. Same as one and two.
[Marcus] Then I'd rather roll four and hold three.
[Priya] I don't love splitting the fleet. Two firmware versions in production is how we end up debugging the wrong thing.
[Marcus] It's already split. Three is behaving differently whether we admit it or not.
[Priya] Fair. Okay, roll four, hold three, and I'll have latency numbers by Thursday.
[Dev] I can pull the per-unit breakdown tonight if that helps.
[Priya] It would. Send it to both of us.
[Marcus] What do we tell the terminal leads?
[Priya] The truth. Site three is holding pending a hardware question, no date yet.
[Marcus] They'll ask for a date.
[Priya] Then say Thursday for a date, not Thursday for a rollout. Those are different sentences and they will hear whichever one we say.
[Dev] Do we need finance in this?
[Priya] Only if we end up replacing the 2019 units. Let's not borrow that yet.
[Marcus] Agreed. Last thing, the install estimate. Finance asked twice.
[Priya] That's on me. I'll get it to them by end of week.
[Marcus] Then we're done.

long_sales_call.transcript:
[Dana, Halloway] I'll be honest, the number came in higher than we budgeted.
[Rob] What did you have penciled?
[Dana] Around forty. You came in at fifty-eight.
[Rob] That fifty-eight includes the migration work. If you did the migration in-house it's forty-four.
[Dana] We don't have anyone to do it in-house until Q1.
[Rob] Then we're comparing forty-four plus your Q1 capacity against fifty-eight now.
[Dana] Put that way it's closer than it looked.
[Rob] I'd also say the migration is where these go wrong. It's not the part I'd hand to a team doing it for the first time.
[Dana] That's fair. What I can't do is sign anything before the board meets on the ninth.
[Rob] Understood. What would you need in front of them?
[Dana] A one-pager. Cost, timeline, and what happens if we do nothing.
[Rob] I can have that Monday. Do you want the do-nothing case honest or gentle?
[Dana] Honest. They've seen gentle.
[Rob] Then I'll put the renewal exposure in it.
[Dana] Do that. And keep the fifty-eight, don't discount it before the meeting. If it drops now they'll assume it drops again.
[Rob] Agreed. One-pager Monday, board on the ninth, no movement on price before then.

long_interview_user_spoke.transcript:
[Interviewer] Tell me about the last thing you shipped that you were proud of.
[Candidate] We replaced the batch importer with a streaming one. The old one held the whole file in memory and fell over above about two hundred megabytes.
[Interviewer] What was hard about it?
[Candidate] Convincing people it was worth doing. It wasn't failing loudly, it was failing for the three biggest customers only, so from the dashboard it looked like a rare edge case.
[Interviewer] How did you make the case?
[Candidate] I pulled the failures by account size instead of by count. Same data, and suddenly it was obviously the top of the market.
